title: A Physical Response-and-Memory Model for Muon Optimization
abstract: arXiv:2608.22994v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Training large language models is costly. How low a loss the same compute can ultimately reach depends on how each step's gradient is converted into a weight update; the rule that performs this conversion is the optimizer. From SGD and AdamW to the recent Muon, effective update rules have mostly been shaped by engineering intuition and then selected on benchmarks. Muon semi-orthogonalizes the momentum matrix before applying the update and has kept breaking records on public training benchmarks; yet why the semi-orthogonalized direction works, and over how long a history the momentum should average, are two questions at present answered mainly by experience. Here we treat the weight matrix during training as a responsive medium with memory and build a physical model for it, in which both questions find answers: the semi-orthogonalized direction is the maximally dissipative response under an output-side safety budget, which explains why

translated_title: 面向Muon优化的物理响应与记忆模型
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.22994v1 公告类型：交叉 摘要：训练大型语言模型成本高昂。在相同的计算量下，最终能达到多低的损失取决于每一步的梯度如何转化为权重更新；执行这一转化的规则就是优化器。从SGD和AdamW到最近的Muon，有效的更新规则大多由工程直觉塑造，然后在基准测试中筛选。Muon在应用更新前对动量矩阵进行半正交化，并持续在公开训练基准上打破记录；然而，为什么半正交化方向有效，以及动量应平均多长的历史，这两个问题目前主要依靠经验来回答。在这里，我们将训练过程中的权重矩阵视为具有记忆的响应介质，并为其构建一个物理模型，在该模型中两个问题都找到了答案：半正交化方向是在输出端安全预算下的最大耗散响应，这解释了为什么...
tldr: 本文提出一个物理模型，将训练中的权重矩阵视为有记忆的响应介质，从而解释Muon优化器中半正交化方向为何有效，并确定了动量平均的最优历史长度。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a physical model treating the weight matrix during training as a responsive medium with memory, explaining why the semi-orthogonalized direction in the Muon optimizer works and determining the optimal momentum averaging history length.
